title: Show-Hands Catching
description: Receivers learn to catch properly: show two hands as a target, step to the ball, catch with soft hands and land ready — the foundation under every pass.

content.objective: Catch every pass with two hands from a ready position, stepping toward the ball and landing balanced.
content.setup: Partners four metres apart; one ball per pair.
content.organization: Pairs; switch roles every eight catches.
instructions: The receiver shows two hands at chest height, fingers up, thumbs almost touching.
The passer calls the receiver's name and passes.
The receiver steps toward the ball and catches it with the fingers, letting the hands give.
Land with a jump stop and bring the ball to the chin.
coachingPoints: Eyes on the ball until it is in the hands.
Step to meet the ball: do not wait for it.
Soft hands: pull the ball in like catching an egg.
commonMistakes: Catching with stiff arms so the ball bounces off.
Turning the head away from the pass.
Standing still and letting the defender jump the pass.
content.safety: Gentle passes for beginners; use a lighter or smaller ball for U8.
progressions: Receiver jogs toward the passer from a starting line.
regressions: Two metres apart with underarm tosses.
Catch, then pause before the pass back.
variations: Catch with a stride stop instead of a jump stop.
Catch one-handed and secure with the second hand.
successCriteria: Every catch finished in a balanced stop.
content.gameApplication: Many turnovers in youth games are fumbled catches; good catching makes every other skill possible.
